note: The main banks were taken as the three largest Polish banks by total assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): PKO Bank Polski, Bank Pekao and Erste Bank Polska (Santander Bank Polska until 2026). PKO Bank Polski: its tariff for individuals, part IV, credit cards on offer (in force from 3 December 2024, the version its card page links today), its rate table (in force from 7 September 2026), its notice of the rate cut from 5 March 2026, and its Przejrzysta card page, read 2026-10-30. All four cards bear a variable 14.50% a year, the NBP reference rate plus 12 points, held at the legal maximum since 5 March 2026; the overdue rate for contracts from 9 January 2016, 18.50%, is written as the penalty rate. The Przejrzysta card is sold as a Visa and as a Mastercard on the same terms, written as two cards. Each card's yearly fee is charged in full below the spending that waives it entirely (7,200, 60,000 and 132,000 zlotys a year); the half fee on lesser spending (40, 150 and 500 zlotys on 6,000, 30,000 and 98,400) isn't written, so the fee is charged in full there. The cash withdrawal fee is 4% (at least 15 zlotys) on the Przejrzysta card, and 3% in Poland on the Platinum and Infinite cards (0% abroad, not written). The currency conversion fee is 4% on the Przejrzysta card and none on the other two. The over-limit fee of 35 zlotys on the Przejrzysta card applies when the limit is exceeded by more than 5%; that threshold isn't modelled, so the fee is charged on any excess. The minimum payment, 4% of the debt and at least 50 zlotys, is the bank's statement for all its credit cards on the card page; the interest-free period of up to 55 days is stated for the Przejrzysta card only. The insurance, express delivery, casino, transfer and certificate charges aren't written. Erste Bank Polska: its tariff for individuals (in force from 25 April 2026), credit cards, table 1, and its card pages, read 2026-10-30. Its four cards on open sale bear a variable 14.50% a year, the legal maximum, as each card page states (at 5 March 2026). The Visa Bonus costs 9 zlotys a month, none after a statement cycle with 300 zlotys of card spending; the Visa Silver 'Akcja Pajacyk', World MasterCard and Visa Platinum cost 7.50, 17.50 and 42 zlotys a month, none after a cycle with ten card transactions, a count the game doesn't check, so their fees are charged in full. Cash withdrawals cost 4%, at least 10 zlotys; foreign-currency spending 2.8% on the Visa Bonus and Visa Silver, none on the World MasterCard and 2% on the Visa Platinum. The minimum payment of 3% of the debt, at least 50 zlotys, is stated on the Visa Bonus page only, and the up to 54 days without interest on the Visa Bonus, Visa Silver and World MasterCard pages; neither is written where its page doesn't state it. The Mastercard World Elite (1,500 zlotys a year, none on 90,000 of spending) is issued only on the bank's invitation and isn't written. The tariff states no late fee or penalty rate for these cards. Bank Pekao's credit card pages and tariff weren't reached: its site's card section didn't come up to a plain fetch, and a search found no current tariff, so its cards aren't written.
